title: Month-end close coordination
benefit: Give the close calendar a current owner, source record, and review status for each task.
tasks: Maintain close tasks and dependencies
Follow up on requested schedules and evidence
Flag late inputs and unresolved review notes
Record authorized sign-offs and handoffs
example: A reconciliation is marked prepared but lacks reviewer sign-off. Support separates those statuses, identifies the reviewer, and keeps the item open until the authorized sign-off is recorded.

faq.question: Can support approve the close?
faq.answer: No. Your finance leadership and qualified accountants retain accounting judgments and final close approval.

photoAlt: Documents and laptops arranged for a team discussion

title: Management reporting support
benefit: Prepare a consistent reporting pack with clear source periods and review notes.
tasks: Refresh approved reporting templates
Label entity, period, and source versions
Collect owner-provided variance explanations
Prepare the approved distribution checklist
example: A report contains figures from two different periods. Support flags the mismatch, attaches each source date, and routes it to the report owner before the pack is approved for distribution.

faq.question: Does support interpret financial performance independently?
faq.answer: Support can organize owner-provided explanations and flag inconsistencies. Financial conclusions and management recommendations stay with your finance leadership.

photoAlt: Colleagues reviewing information on a laptop

title: Reconciliation workflow support
benefit: Keep supporting schedules, unresolved differences, and reviewer sign-offs connected.
tasks: Organize reconciliations by account and period
Attach approved supporting evidence
Maintain an aged exception list
Track preparation and review status separately
example: A supporting schedule differs from the ledger export. Support records the difference and source versions, routes it to the account owner, and leaves the resolution open for qualified review.

faq.question: Can support create balancing entries?
faq.answer: Only your authorized accounting professionals determine and approve accounting entries. Support documents differences and maintains the review trail.

photoAlt: Hands checking a calculation against written records

title: Accounts payable controls support
benefit: Keep invoice, vendor, and approval records organized before the authorized payment decision.
tasks: Track invoices and missing supporting records
Maintain the documented approval trail
Flag duplicate references and vendor-data exceptions
Prepare approved payment-review queues
example: An invoice contains new bank details. Support flags the change under the vendor-control procedure and holds it for authorized verification instead of updating the vendor record from the invoice alone.

faq.question: Can support release payments?
faq.answer: Payment authorization and release stay with your designated finance personnel. This service organizes records and approval status.

photoAlt: Colleagues reviewing financial documents at a table

title: Accounts receivable operations
benefit: Keep invoicing, account follow-up, and disputed items visible in one working queue.
tasks: Prepare invoice inputs from approved records
Maintain customer follow-up worklists
Record approved reminders and replies
Route disputes, credits, and corrections for review
example: A customer questions a line on an invoice. Support records the disputed item and source reference, pauses further messaging when your procedure requires it, and routes the question to the account owner.

faq.question: Can support approve credits or settlements?
faq.answer: No. Credits, write-offs, settlements, and changes to commercial terms require your authorized finance or account owner.

photoAlt: Financial records being reviewed with a calculator and laptop

title: Cash visibility support
benefit: Maintain a dated view of approved cash inputs and unresolved timing assumptions.
tasks: Update approved cash schedules
Label source dates and expected receipt or payment timing
Collect assumptions from accountable owners
Flag missing inputs and changes for finance review
example: An expected receipt moves to a later date. Support records the owner’s revised timing, marks the assumption change, and routes the updated schedule for finance review before circulation.

faq.question: Is this treasury or investment advice?
faq.answer: No. Support maintains approved schedules and documentation. Funding, investment, liquidity, and treasury decisions remain with your authorized professionals.

photoAlt: Financial statements, checklist, and calculator on a desk

title: Finance process documentation
benefit: Make recurring finance procedures clear enough for a new owner to follow and a reviewer to inspect.
tasks: Capture steps from process owners
Document source systems and approval points
Maintain version histories and exception paths
Prepare walkthrough notes and unresolved questions
example: During a walkthrough, two teams name different owners for the same approval. Support records the conflict and waits for finance leadership to designate responsibility before finalizing the procedure.

faq.question: Does a documented procedure certify compliance?
faq.answer: No. Documentation makes the operating process visible. Control design, compliance conclusions, audit work, and professional assurance remain with your qualified advisers.

photoAlt: Colleagues reviewing documents together at a laptop

title: Budget and forecast coordination
benefit: Collect department inputs and keep forecast versions ready for finance review.
tasks: Maintain the budget calendar and department input checklist
Collect approved assumptions and supporting schedules
Check template completeness and identify version mismatches
Track finance review comments and revised submissions
prep: Approved budget templates and planning dates
example: One department updates its headcount plan after submitting its forecast. Support identifies the affected workbook version, requests the revised approved input, and flags the change to finance before consolidation.

faq.question: Who owns the forecast assumptions?
faq.answer: Your department leaders and finance team approve assumptions, accounting treatment, and the final forecast. Support collects inputs, maintains versions, and documents review status.
